title: Stacks and stacked diffs
author: Graphite
version: 2026-11-14; the address is the publisher's documentation root and was not fetched in this container, so the revision is named rather than read

record.source: A stack is a run of dependent units where each commit carries the one below it as its base, so rewriting a lower unit rewrites the units above it. Graphite, Sapling, Jujutsu (`jj`) and git-branchless publish the same method under different names, and each automates the restack.
record.kept: The method: a unit is a commit, a dependent run is a stack, and a correction to a lower unit restacks the units above it. This is the grain the convention's fold, the protocol's iteration commit and the change model's early change each name.
record.rewritten: The tool. The repository uses plain git -- a correction folds with `git rebase --autosquash`, and a stack is the branch tree `references/branching.md` states -- so no stack manager is adopted and no history is restacked outside the session that made it.
record.added: The workflow rules no stack tool states, because they are policy rather than mechanics: which actor rules on a correction, and that a correction never rewrites published history.
record.dropped: The hosted review surface and the rebase-on-update automation. The host's verbs own the accept path, and the branch is prepared before it reaches them.
